accepted.s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
o: Amritlal Thakkar
Madan Mohan Malaviya
G.D. Birla
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
accepted.x: G.D. Birla served as the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh, while Amritlal Thakkar was its secretary.
accepted.tq: Use the office-holder distinction to avoid confusing president with secretary.
accepted.sec: Harijan Sevak Sangh - founder, former name, president, year

accepted.s: Amritlal Thakkar, popularly known as Thakkar Bapa, was associated with the Harijan Sevak Sangh as its:
o: Andhra branch president
Secretary
Founder
First president
accepted.x: Amritlal Thakkar, popularly known as Thakkar Bapa, was the secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated office-bearers.
accepted.sec: Harijan Sevak Sangh - founder, former name, president, year

accepted.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in September 1932. A specific record places its establishment on:
o: 30 October 1932 at Mumbai
2 October 1932 at Wardha
26 November 1932 at Delhi
24 September 1932 at Poona
accepted.x: The organisation was founded in September 1932; one record specifically gives 30 October 1932 at Mumbai as the date and place of establishment.
accepted.tq: Separate the general month from the specifically recorded date and place.
accepted.sec: Harijan Sevak Sangh - founder, former name, president, year

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the activities associated with the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
o: Establishing schools and hostels
Introducing separate electorates for the Depressed Classes
Encouraging inter-dining and inter-caste marriage
Promoting entry into wells and temples
accepted.x: The Sangh worked for access to wells, schools and temples, and promoted schools, hostels, cooperatives, inter-dining and inter-caste marriage. Separate electorates were a political demand associated with the Poona Pact debate, not its activity.
accepted.tq: Find the option belonging to the political debate rather than the organisation's constructive work.
accepted.sec: Harijan Sevak Sangh - founder, former name, president, year

accepted.s: Which pair relating to the Andhra branches of the Harijan Sevak Sangh is correctly matched?
o: Hyderabad—Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao; Vijayawada—Maganti Bapineedu
Vijayawada—Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao; Hyderabad—Maganti Bapineedu
Vijayawada—G.D. Birla; Hyderabad—Amritlal Thakkar
Hyderabad—Durgabai; Vijayawada—Kolla Tayaramma
accepted.x: The Andhra branches were located at Hyderabad and Vijayawada. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was president and Maganti Bapineedu was secretary of the Vijayawada branch.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure branch-office bearer pair.
accepted.sec: Harijan Sevak Sangh - founder, former name, president, year

accepted.s: Nai Talim, or Basic Education, primarily aimed at:
o: Replacing manual work with purely literary education
Providing higher education exclusively in English
Training students only for government employment
Making villages self-sufficient through vocational and craft-centred education
accepted.x: Gandhi's Basic Education was vocational and craft-centred, sought to make villages self-sufficient and aimed to dignify manual labour.
accepted.tq: Identify the educational philosophy from its practical social objective.
accepted.sec: Nai Talim - Wardha Scheme, Zakir Hussain Committee

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education:
1. The Wardha Educational Conference adopted the scheme in 1937.
2. The Zakir Hussain Committee drew up the scheme.
3. The scheme prescribed free and compulsory education for seven years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme was adopted in 1937, drafted by the Zakir Hussain Committee, and envisaged seven years of free and compulsory education.
accepted.tq: Check the date, drafting committee and duration before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Nai Talim - Wardha Scheme, Zakir Hussain Committee

accepted.s: Under Nai Talim, the proposed age group for seven years of free and compulsory education was:
o: 5–10 years
8–16 years
6–12 years
7–14 years
accepted.x: Nai Talim proposed seven years of free and compulsory education for children in the age group of 7 to 14 years.
accepted.tq: Test the paired duration and age range precisely.
accepted.sec: Nai Talim - Wardha Scheme, Zakir Hussain Committee

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principle of Nai Talim?
o: Exclusive reliance on classical languages
Mother-tongue medium
Dignity of manual labour
Learning through a productive craft
accepted.x: Nai Talim emphasised the mother tongue, productive craft and dignity of manual labour; it did not prescribe exclusive reliance on classical languages.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the practical and vernacular character of the scheme.
accepted.sec: Nai Talim - Wardha Scheme, Zakir Hussain Committee

accepted.s:
With reference to the temple-entry movements, consider the following pairs:
a. Vaikom — Travancore
b. Guruvayur — Malabar
c. Siddhantam — Krishna district
d. Lakshminarayan Temple — Wardha
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: a and b only
a, b and c only
b, c and d only
a, b, c and d
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Vaikom was in Travancore, Guruvayur in Malabar, Siddhantam in Krishna district and the Lakshminarayan Temple was at Wardha.
accepted.tq: Match each movement with its location before checking the combined code.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924–25 was associated with which combination?
o: T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon; Gandhi visited and negotiated
Potti Sriramulu and Durgabai; Gandhi organised the procession
Jamnalal Bajaj and Malaviya; Gandhi led the fast
K. Kelappan and A.K. Gopalan; Gandhi ordered the opening of the temple
accepted.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha in Travancore was led by T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon. Periyar participated, Sree Narayana Guru supported it, and Gandhi visited and negotiated.
accepted.tq: Use the leader-role distinction: Gandhi negotiated rather than being listed as the principal local leader.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: Who took part in the Vaikom Satyagraha, while Sree Narayana Guru supported it?
o: Jamnalal Bajaj
K. Kelappan
Periyar E.V. Ramasamy
A.K. Gopalan
accepted.x: Periyar took part in the Vaikom Satyagraha, and Sree Narayana Guru extended support to the movement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish participation from leadership in related temple-entry movements.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, year, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Guruvayur Satyagraha is correct?
o: It was an Andhra movement led by Siddhantam Congress leaders.
It took place in Travancore during 1924–25.
It opened the Lakshminarayan Temple to Dalits in 1928.
It took place in Malabar during 1931–32, with K. Kelappan undertaking a fast.
accepted.x: The Guruvayur Satyagraha took place in Malabar in 1931–32. K. Kelappan fasted and A.K. Gopalan was associated with the movement; Gandhi asked Kelappan to end his fast.
accepted.tq: Separate the place and dates of Guruvayur from those of Vaikom.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, year, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: The Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha was opened to Dalits in 1928 by:
o: K. Kelappan
Madan Mohan Malaviya
Jamnalal Bajaj
Amritlal Thakkar
accepted.x: Jamnalal Bajaj opened the Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha to Dalits in 1928.
accepted.tq: Apply the founder-or-doer trap to a temple-entry reform.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, year, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: Siddhantam temple entry movement, an early Andhra initiative, took place in which year and district?
o: 1931, Malabar district
1936, Nellore district
1928, Wardha district
1933, Krishna district
accepted.x: Siddhantam was an early Andhra temple-entry movement led by Congress leaders in Krishna district in 1933.
accepted.tq: Use the Andhra-specific place-year combination to eliminate nearby movements.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, year, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the Indian National Congress reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under:
o: Amritlal Thakkar
B.R. Ambedkar
Madan Mohan Malaviya
G.D. Birla
accepted.x: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the INC reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
accepted.tq: Test the person placed in charge rather than the movement associated with the issue.
accepted.sec: Temple entry satyagrahas - place, year, leaders, Gandhi's role

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Gandhi's Harijan tour?
o: November 1933 to July 1934, covering about 20,000 km from Wardha Ashram
August 1934 to March 1935, covering about 10,000 km from Sabarmati
January 1933 to December 1933, covering about 5,000 km from Poona
November 1932 to July 1933, covering about 20,000 km from Mumbai
accepted.x: Gandhi's Harijan tour ran from November 1933 to July 1934, covered about 20,000 km, began from the Wardha Ashram and collected funds for the Harijan Sevak Sangh. Orthodox groups disrupted some meetings.
accepted.tq: Combine the duration, distance, starting point and purpose instead of relying on a single date.
accepted.sec: Harijan weekly and Harijan tour

accepted.s: The term ‘Harijan’, meaning ‘children of God’, was taken from the writings or usage associated with:
o: Narsi Mehta
Kabir
Sree Narayana Guru
Jyotirao Phule
accepted.x: Gandhi adopted the term ‘Harijan’, meaning ‘children of God’, from the Gujarati saint Narsi Mehta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the source of a term from later critics of its usage.
accepted.sec: Harijan weekly and Harijan tour

accepted.s: Gandhi described untouchability as:
o: A necessary feature of village organisation
A political question unrelated to religion
A blot on Hinduism
A temporary form of economic inequality
accepted.x: Gandhi called untouchability ‘a blot on Hinduism’ and advocated reform from within Hindu society.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact quotation rather than a broad paraphrase.
accepted.sec: Gandhi on untouchability - quotations, route to uplift

accepted.s: Which of the following represents Gandhi's route for the uplift of communities subjected to untouchability?
o: Separate electorates, political boycott and armed resistance
Exclusive reliance on litigation and legislative vetoes
Moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work
Economic isolation of orthodox Hindu groups
accepted.x: Gandhi's approach combined moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete constructive programme rather than a single method.
accepted.sec: Gandhi on untouchability - quotations, route to uplift

accepted.s: The Congress ministries after 1937 are associated with which measure concerning Harijans?
o: Compulsory separate electorates
A ban on temple entry campaigns
Free education for Harijans
Abolition of all caste identities by executive order
accepted.x: After 1937, Congress ministries provided free education to Harijans as part of their social reform measures.
accepted.tq: Match the historical period with the specific administrative measure.
accepted.sec: Gandhi on untouchability - quotations, route to uplift

accepted.s: Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as:
o: Paternalistic and weak on civil rights
Opposed to education and hostel facilities
Too radical in demanding separate electorates
A purely religious organisation with no social programme
accepted.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma considered the Sangh paternalistic and criticised it for being weak on civil rights.
accepted.tq: Test the exact nature of the criticism rather than the organisation's stated activities.
accepted.sec: Gandhi on untouchability - quotations, route to uplift

accepted.s: Which statement best distinguishes Gandhi's position on varna from his position on untouchability?
o: Gandhi regarded untouchability as the purest form of varna.
Gandhi considered caste and untouchability identical in every respect.
Gandhi regarded varna ideally as a division of labour but considered untouchability a corruption.
Gandhi rejected all forms of social organisation but supported untouchability.
accepted.x: Gandhi distinguished ideal varna as a division of labour from untouchability, which he regarded as a corruption.
accepted.tq: Separate two closely related concepts instead of treating them as synonyms.
accepted.sec: Caste - varna vs untouchability; debate with Ambedkar

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the contrast between Gandhi and Ambedkar on caste?
o: Gandhi advocated annihilation of caste, whereas Ambedkar defended the existing caste system.
Gandhi sought reform of varna, whereas Ambedkar advocated annihilation of the caste system.
Both regarded the existing caste system as ideal and unchangeable.
Both confined their approaches exclusively to temple entry.
accepted.x: Gandhi viewed varna ideally as a division of labour, while Ambedkar regarded the whole caste system as oppressive and advocated its annihilation.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish the two thinkers.
accepted.sec: Caste - varna vs untouchability; debate with Ambedkar

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gandhi — Harijan
2. Ambedkar — Dalit / Scheduled Castes
3. Gandhi — Moral persuasion and temple entry
4. Ambedkar — Legal, constitutional and political rights
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Gandhi used the term Harijan and stressed moral persuasion and temple entry, while Ambedkar preferred Dalit or Scheduled Castes and emphasised legal, constitutional and political rights.
accepted.tq: Match each thinker with both terminology and method before choosing the full combination.
accepted.sec: Caste - varna vs untouchability; debate with Ambedkar

accepted.s: Which statement accurately describes the positions of Gandhi and Ambedkar during the Poona Pact episode?
o: Ambedkar fasted against joint electorates, while Gandhi accepted separate electorates.
Gandhi fasted against separate electorates, while Ambedkar accepted joint electorates with more reserved seats.
Gandhi demanded separate electorates, while Ambedkar opposed all reservations.
Both demanded separate electorates and rejected reserved seats.
accepted.x: Gandhi fasted against separate electorates. Ambedkar accepted joint electorates with more reserved seats in order to save Gandhi's life.
accepted.tq: Track the change from separate electorates to joint electorates with reserved seats.
accepted.sec: Caste - varna vs untouchability; debate with Ambedkar

accepted.s: Which of the following activities brought women into the Gandhian satyagraha movement?
o: Serving only as members of legislative councils
Picketing liquor shops, making salt and facing lathi charges
Restricting participation to spinning within the home
Avoiding all public demonstrations
accepted.x: Gandhi brought women into public action through activities such as picketing liquor shops, making salt and facing lathis.
accepted.tq: Recognise the concrete activities that indicate public participation in satyagraha.
accepted.sec: Women - satyagraha, purdah, child marriage, widows

accepted.s: Gandhi opposed which of the following social practices and supported remarriage of child widows?
o: Purdah, child marriage and dowry
Inter-dining, widow remarriage and basic education
Khadi, salt-making and public prayer
Temple entry, female education and village industries
accepted.x: Gandhi opposed purdah, child marriage and dowry, and supported the remarriage of child widows.
accepted.tq: Group the practices by Gandhi's reform position and reject unrelated constructive activities.
accepted.sec: Women - satyagraha, purdah, child marriage, widows

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding women's participation in Andhra is correct?
o: Desasevikalu functioned as a women's wing, and Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921.
Durgabai met Gandhi at Wardha in 1937 and opposed the Tilak Fund.
Women in Andhra contributed only labour and not jewellery to nationalist causes.
Desasevikalu was a Harijan men's organisation formed in Nellore in 1946.
accepted.x: Desasevikalu was a women's wing. Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921, raised Rs 5,000, and Andhra women donated jewellery to the Tilak Fund.
accepted.tq: Combine the organisation, place, year and contribution to identify the precise statement.
accepted.sec: Women - satyagraha, purdah, child marriage, widows

accepted.s: Sarva dharma samabhava signifies:
o: Separation of religion from all public prayer
The superiority of one religion over all others
Acceptance of only reformist Hindu sects
Equal respect for all religions
accepted.x: Sarva dharma samabhava means equal respect for all religions. Gandhi's ashram prayers drew upon several faiths.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of the Sanskrit expression.
accepted.sec: Religion - sarva dharma samabhava, unity, prayers

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects Gandhi's view of Hindu-Muslim unity?
o: It was the bedrock of nationalism, and Gandhi supported the Khilafat movement.
It was limited to private prayer and not public action.
It was unrelated to nationalism, and Gandhi opposed the Khilafat movement.
It required the political dominance of one religious community.
accepted.x: Gandhi regarded Hindu-Muslim unity as the bedrock of nationalism and supported the Khilafat movement.
accepted.tq: Link the principle with the associated political action.
accepted.sec: Religion - sarva dharma samabhava, unity, prayers

accepted.s: Gandhi undertook fasts during communal riots in which places during 1946–47?
o: Calcutta and Noakhali
Vaikom and Guruvayur
Tenali and Nellore
Wardha and Poona
accepted.x: Gandhi fasted during communal disturbances in Calcutta and Noakhali in 1946–47.
accepted.tq: Match the place pair with the correct period and purpose.
accepted.sec: Religion - sarva dharma samabhava, unity, prayers

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Gandhi's work in Andhra is correctly matched?
o: Kolla Tayaramma — Tenali; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Nellore
Kolla Tayaramma — Nellore; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Tenali
Kolla Tayaramma — Kakinada; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Vijayawada
Kolla Tayaramma — Machilipatnam; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Wardha
accepted.x: Kolla Tayaramma led Harijan schools and hostels at Tenali, while Alladi Annapurna Devi was associated with similar work at Nellore.
accepted.tq: Start with the place-person pair and eliminate the reversed match.
accepted.sec: Gandhi in Andhra - Harijan and khadi tours

accepted.s: Gandhi's work in Andhra included which combination?
o: Collecting funds for Harijan work, campaigning against untouchability, visiting Machilipatnam for Swaraj Nidhi and promoting Ponduru khadi
Organising the Poona Pact and drafting the Zakir Hussain Committee report
Leading the Vaikom Satyagraha and founding the Lakshminarayan Temple
Starting the Khilafat movement in Noakhali and Calcutta
accepted.x: Gandhi toured Andhra extensively for Harijan uplift and anti-untouchability work, visited Machilipatnam for Swaraj Nidhi and was associated with Ponduru khadi.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing only Andhra-specific activities.
accepted.sec: Gandhi in Andhra - Harijan and khadi tours

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the constitutional significance of Gandhi's anti-untouchability campaign is correct?
o: The Constitution abolished caste itself through Article 17.
It kept untouchability outside the constitutional framework.
Article 17 constitutionally protected untouchability as a customary practice.
It helped make untouchability a national issue, and the Constitution abolished untouchability through Article 17.
accepted.x: Gandhi's campaign made untouchability a national issue, and Article 17 of the Constitution abolished untouchability. Article 17 did not abolish the entire caste system.
accepted.tq: Avoid the Article-number and scope trap by distinguishing untouchability from caste.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed, in the context of the Sabarimala reference, that untouchability:
o: May be practised for three days a month
Was abolished only in temple premises
Is exclusively a matter for religious authorities
Cannot be practised even three days a month
accepted.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that untouchability cannot be practised ‘three days a month’ in the Sabarimala reference.
accepted.tq: Test the exact qualification in a judicial observation rather than its broad theme.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the stated 2026 observance or initiative?
o: PM-AJAY — development of SC habitations
Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary — 28 August 2026
Sree Narayana Guru's 172nd birth anniversary — 11 April 2026
PM-AJAY — promotion of separate electorates
accepted.x: PM-AJAY provides funds for development of SC habitations. Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on 11 April 2026, while Sree Narayana Guru's 172nd birth anniversary was on 28 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the scheme's purpose from the anniversary dates in the same theme.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on:
o: 28 August 2026
11 April 2026
24 September 2026
8 April 2026
accepted.x: Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on 11 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related social-reform anniversary dates.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement about criticism of Gandhi's terminology and approach is correct?
o: Dalit leaders rejected constitutional rights but supported paternalism.
Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term ‘Harijan’ and criticised caste-Hindu paternalism.
Ambedkar accepted ‘Harijan’ as the preferred political designation.
The criticism was directed only against khadi and not against caste reform.
accepted.x: Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term ‘Harijan’ and criticised what they regarded as caste-Hindu paternalism.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reform programme from the terminology and power-relationship critique.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Potti Sriramulu's temple-entry fasts in Nellore are associated with which year?
accepted.x: Potti Sriramulu undertook temple-entry fasts in Nellore in 1946. Accounts differ on the precise duration, reporting 23 days in one source and a 10-day followed by a 19-day sequence in another.
accepted.tq: Use the year while avoiding an uncertain duration claim.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
